strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation distinguishing proactive (SRGen) from reactive error correction approaches
Strong theoretical grounding through Theorem 1 showing the hybrid loss is equivalent to constrained optimization with Pareto-optimality interpretation
Comprehensive experimental validation across 4 diverse models (7B-32B, multiple architectures) and 6 benchmarks with consistent improvements
Practical plug-and-play applicability without training, demonstrable composability with other methods (SLOT), and bounded computational overhead
Thorough efficiency analysis (Section 5.3) showing overhead scales only with intervention count, not sequence length
Insightful analysis of triggered tokens (Section 5.6) validating that interventions target decision-critical function words rather than content tokens
Compelling demonstration that dynamic thresholding is necessary (Appendix F) with entropy profiles varying dramatically across models
Robust to hyperparameter variations (Appendix G: ±1% stability across reasonable ranges)
weaknesses: Moderate technical novelty—combines existing components (entropy detection, hidden state injection, dual-objective losses) rather than introducing fundamentally new mechanisms
Restrictive white-box requirement (hidden state and gradient access) severely limits real-world deployment on API-only production models, undermining practical claims

Design choices inadequately justified: (1) dynamic threshold form (µ+kσ) lacks comparison to alternative anomaly detection methods; (2) entropy minimization objective not compared to other uncertainty metrics; (3) uniform δ application to all historical states (Eq. 6) lacks ablation against localized variants
No quantitative analysis of intervention quality: missing false-positive rate, intervention success rate, and precision/recall of uncertainty detection
Theoretical assumptions not fully validated: coercivity for minimizer existence unverified; Joint-Descent Lemma's acute-angle requirement breaks down after early optimization steps (Fig. 9)

Experimental limitations: (1) no confidence intervals despite 'five runs'; (2) lack of significance testing with some improvements modest (e.g., +0.7±3.3 on AIME2025); (3) inconsistent decoding setup (greedy vs. temperature 0.6) across tables

Limited evaluation scope: all benchmarks are mathematics/reasoning-heavy; no evaluation on generation tasks (summarization, translation) where entropy patterns differ; function-word triggering pattern may be task-specific
Multiple hyperparameters (6 total: k, N, λ, T, η, τ) with non-obvious defaults; paper acknowledges 'best performance may vary' requiring per-task tuning
Missing critical ablations: alternative loss formulations, threshold mechanisms, contextual fidelity implementations, and temperature sensitivity beyond Appendix F

Incomplete technical specification: ring buffer initialization when |E| < N undefined, stopping criterion for δ optimization vague ('a few steps'), clarification of historical vs. current δ injection (Algorithm 1, line 15)

strengths: Novel conceptual framing of proactive, test-time self-reflection as a distinct paradigm from reactive post-hoc and training-based approaches, with clear positioning via Table 1

Solid theoretical foundation: Theorem 1 elegantly shows the hybrid loss is equivalent to Lagrangian relaxation of a principled constrained optimization problem, and the Joint-Descent Lemma provides theoretical justification for optimization dynamics

Comprehensive experimental validation across diverse models (7B-32B, Qwen/DeepSeek architectures) and multiple benchmark types (math, general reasoning, code) with consistently strong gains (5-12 pp on AIME)
Strong practical design with dynamic entropy thresholding that adapts to model/temperature/task and scales overhead with intervention count rather than sequence length

Thorough experimental practices: detailed efficiency analysis (Figure 2, Table 3), comprehensive ablation studies (Appendix G), demonstration of orthogonality with SLOT, and provided prompts/hyperparameters for reproducibility

Insightful analysis showing that critical tokens cluster around discourse connectives and decision points (Figure 4), with empirical validation of theoretical predictions about the joint-descent regime (Figures 8-9)
Clear presentation with well-motivated problem, effective figures, and transparent methodology; case studies demonstrate concrete error correction mechanisms
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: combines existing techniques (dynamic entropy thresholding, corrective vectors in hidden states from SLOT, standard hybrid loss) rather than introducing fundamentally new algorithms or theory

Restricted to white-box access despite 'plug-and-play' framing; inapplicable to API-only models (GPT-4, Claude), increasingly the dominant deployment paradigm, substantially constraining practical impact

Uncertain generalization beyond mathematical reasoning: gains on GPQA (1.3-2.2 pp) and EvalPlus (0.6-1.9 pp) are modest, with no experiments on other domains (multi-hop QA, dialogue, summarization); paper does not analyze why performance varies across domains

Introduces 6 hyperparameters (k, N, λ, T, η, τ) with unclear guidance for de novo selection on new models/tasks; defaults may not transfer across domains, undermining 'plug-and-play' and 'bounded overhead' claims

Limited mechanistic understanding of why intervention works: paper shows that high-entropy token intervention helps but provides minimal insight into semantic mechanisms or failure modes; no analysis of confident-but-wrong errors

Entropy-based uncertainty detection has blind spots: assumes high entropy signals error risk, but confident errors (high probability on incorrect token) evade detection; no comparison with other uncertainty quantification methods or measurement of false negative rates

Experimental scope limitations: primarily uses greedy decoding or temperature 0.6 (unclear generalization to diverse sampling or exploration); overhead analysis limited to one model-task pair (Qwen2.5-Math-7B on MATH500); only 5 runs reported without statistical significance testing

Theoretical contributions are relatively standard: Theorem 1's constrained optimization ↔ Lagrangian equivalence is well-known; Joint-Descent Lemma lacks theoretical justification; no formal guarantees on improvement conditions or convergence analysis

Computational overhead not fully characterized: trigger frequency across domains not systematically studied; peak memory increase of +13% (15.7 → 17.8 GB) is non-trivial; cost breakdown in Equation 10 depends on Nact, which lacks systematic analysis
